title.zh: 像素主播 MirrorStudio：AI 数字人带货

theme.zh: 生成内容标识、肖像授权与深度伪造
theme.en: Generated-content labelling, likeness rights and deepfakes

product.zh: 一套数字人直播工具：商家录三分钟视频（或选用模板形象），系统就能生成一位可以整晚不停播的带货主播，自动讲解商品、回答常见问题。
product.en: A digital-host livestream tool: a merchant records three minutes (or picks a template face) and the system produces a shopping host who can stream all night, presenting products and answering common questions.

customer.zh: 请不起真人主播、又想守住夜间时段的小微商家与连锁门店；MCN 机构要的是批量定制版。
customer.en: Small merchants and chain stores that cannot afford a human host but want to cover the night shift; MCN agencies want bespoke versions in bulk.

standing.zh: 第一位付费客户已经跑通，团队正准备把工具产品化；收费模式尚未定型。
standing.en: The first paying customer is live and the team is about to productise the tool; pricing is not settled.

data.zh: 真人的肖像与声音素材（属生物特征信息），以及由此生成的合成内容。合成内容通常须显著标识并保留可追溯元数据；否则极易被用于冒充与诈骗。
data.en: Real people's faces and voices (biometric material), plus the synthetic content made from them. Synthetic content normally must be clearly labelled with traceable metadata; without it, impersonation and fraud follow easily.

act1.zh: 第一章 · 客群与问题（Canvas 1–2）

act2.zh: 第二章 · 方案、数据与模型训练（Canvas 3–4）
act2.en: Act II · Solution, Data and Training (Canvas 3–4)

act3.zh: 第三章 · 渠道、收入与问责（Canvas 5–8）
act3.en: Act III · Channels, Revenue and Accountability (Canvas 5–8)

act4.zh: 第四章 · 规模化与社会外溢（Canvas 7、9）

text.zh: 你们的第一个客户是一家连锁早餐店。上线两周，夜间直播间的成交额比老板真人播的时候还高。评论区有人问：主播是请来的小姑娘吗？老板回了一个笑脸。
text.en: Your first customer is a breakfast-shop chain. Two weeks after launch, the late-night stream outsells the owner's own sessions. Someone asks in the comments whether the host is a hired presenter. The owner replies with a smiley.

text.zh: 接下第二批客户，把工具产品化
text.en: Sign the second batch of customers and productise the tool

text.zh: 第一件事：先把工具卖给谁？本地生活商家铺满了整条街，而品牌方的预算在一个完全不同的量级。
text.en: First question: who do you sell to first? Local merchants line the whole street, while brand budgets live in a completely different league.

text.zh: 深耕本地生活商家：餐饮、零售、服务门店
text.en: Go deep on local merchants: food, retail and service shops

why.zh: 同一类商家的带货话术与货品结构相似，容易形成可复用的模板与效果基准；这类口碑一旦铺开就是最难被抄走的资产（Canvas 9），只是单价很低。
why.en: One merchant category shares scripts and product structures, so templates and benchmarks become reusable; that reputation, once localised, is the hardest asset to copy (Canvas 9) — though unit prices stay low.

text.zh: 面向所有带货场景，先把播主数量做起来
text.en: Serve every live-commerce scenario and scale the number of avatars

why.zh: 海量用户意味着海量面孔与声音样本，而你既没有时间逐一核实授权，也很难监督每个数字人最终出现在什么场景。规模来得最快，失控也最快。
why.en: Mass adoption means mass volumes of faces and voices, with neither time to verify each licence nor visibility into where every avatar eventually appears. Scale arrives fastest, and so does loss of control.

text.zh: 第二件事：商家的真痛点是什么？有人说请不起主播，也有运营说真正缺的是「有人盯屏」。就在这时候，一家 MCN 机构找上门：他们要一整套定制版，愿意先付一年的钱。
text.en: Second question: what is the merchant's real pain? Some say they cannot afford a host; one operator says what they really lack is 'someone watching the stream'. Right then an MCN agency comes knocking: they want a bespoke version and will pay a year up front.

text.zh: 跟十五家门店聊，确认痛点是夜间时段无人值守
text.en: Interview fifteen stores; confirm the pain is unstaffed night hours

why.zh: 把问题定义为「夜间空档」而不是「主播太贵」，产品的边界就清楚了：补齐时段而非替代人。Canvas 2 的证据越扎实，后续的功能与定价越容易说服人。
why.en: Framing the problem as 'dead night hours' rather than 'hosts are expensive' clarifies scope: fill the slot, do not replace the person. Stronger Canvas 2 evidence makes features and pricing far easier to defend.

text.zh: 做一键「明星脸」主播，用酷炫效果拉新
text.en: Ship one-click celebrity-look hosts and acquire users with spectacle

why.zh: 皮肤与形象的噱头确实能带来疯传式增长。但允许生成与现实公众人物高度相似的形象，通常落在肖像权、声音权益与反不正当竞争的交叉区，也最容易被用于误导。
why.en: Spectacle around looks and voices really does spread fast. But letting users generate likenesses close to real public figures lands squarely on the overlap of portrait rights, voice rights and unfair competition — and is easiest to misuse.

text.zh: 按最大客户要求做：给一家 MCN 做专属定制版
text.en: Build what the biggest client wants: a bespoke version for one MCN

why.zh: 一个定制大单让 Canvas 6 立刻成立，现金流确定。但产品会朝单一机构的直播间诉求偏移，中小商家的真实痛点被排在后面，契合度下降。
why.en: One bespoke deal makes Canvas 6 work immediately and removes cash doubt. But the roadmap bends towards one studio's studio-stage needs, pushing real merchant pain further down — fit drops.

text.zh: MVP 二选一：每位商家拥有自己的数字人，还是所有人共用一套更好看的模板？
text.en: Two MVP candidates: every merchant gets their own digital host, or everyone shares one better-looking template?

text.zh: 品牌专属数字人：需本人出镜授权、录满三分钟
text.en: Brand-exclusive avatars requiring the person to appear and authorise a three-minute recording

why.zh: 要求本人出镜并签署授权，会让上手流程变重、转化变慢；但这套授权凭证与唯一的音色−形象配对，恰是日后抵御盗用指控、拿下品牌客户的资产（Canvas 9）。
why.en: Requiring appearance and written authorisation makes onboarding heavy and conversion slow; but those consent records and unique voice-likeness pairings are exactly what defends you against impersonation claims and wins brand clients (Canvas 9).

text.zh: 共享模板 + 一键生成：不要求实名，先款先得
text.en: Shared templates with one-click generation: no identity checks, first come first served

why.zh: 零门槛带来最快的用户增长。但当任何人都能生成以假乱真的面孔与声音，这些素材进入公共信息环境的速度与规模，本身就是一类难以回收的公共风险。
why.en: Zero friction brings the fastest user growth. But once anyone can generate indistinguishable faces and voices, the speed and scale at which such clips enter the public information space is itself a hard-to-recall public risk.

text.zh: 要让数字人自然，需要大量真人的形象与声音素材。签约模特要钱；网上有大量网红视频可以「取」。
text.en: To make avatars look natural you need lots of real faces and voices. Signing models costs money; the internet is full of influencer footage you could 'borrow'.

text.zh: 签约本地模特与学生，签署明确的肖像与声音授权
text.en: Sign local models and students with explicit likeness and voice licences

why.zh: 授权素材数量有限会限制初期效果，但每一份明示授权都能追溯到人，后续商用、转授权、出海都不会埋雷。这是一种慢但干净的底料。
why.en: Licensed material is limited, which caps early quality, but every explicit consent traces back to a person, so later commercial use, sublicensing and expansion carry no buried liabilities. Slow, but clean feedstock.

text.zh: 抓取网红直播片段做训练集，先做出效果
text.en: Scrape influencer streams for the training set and get results first

why.zh: 未经许可的形象与声音属于受保护的人格权益，用它训练会直接种下侵权与非法生物特征处理的隐患；若素材中夹杂公职人员或敏感场景，后果更重。效果确实提升。
why.en: Unauthorised likeness and voice are protected personality interests; training on them plants the seed for infringement and unlawful biometric processing claims. It is worse still if the footage includes public officials or sensitive settings. It does improve output quality.

text.zh: 口型与微表情总要更多数据才够自然。合规同学建议只用授权数据，工程同学说数据量不够。
text.en: Lip sync and micro-expressions ease when you have more data. Compliance wants authorised data only; engineering says there is not enough.

text.zh: 只用授权数据，接受口型略逊的版本
text.en: Use authorised data only and accept slightly worse lip sync

why.zh: 效果略差会让演示没那么惊艳，但每一项数据的来源都能被写进技术文档；这在投标、尽调与平台审核时是最省时间的通行证。
why.en: Slightly weaker output makes demos less impressive, but every datum's provenance can go into the technical documentation — the most time-saving pass there is in bidding, diligence and platform review.

text.zh: 混入第三方素材库与网络抓到的样本
text.en: Blend in third-party libraries and scraped samples

why.zh: 混合数据集通常交付出最好的效果指标，但你无法证明每一条的合法性基础；一旦有人主张权利，举证责任与追溯成本都在你们这边。
why.en: Mixed datasets usually produce the best quality metrics, but you cannot prove a lawful basis for each item; when someone asserts their rights, both the burden of proof and the tracing cost fall on you.

text.zh: 客服转来一条投诉：有人用你们的模板做了某位财经评论员的形象，在群聊里推荐所谓「稳赚」的投资群。
text.en: Support forwards a complaint: someone used your templates to build the likeness of a financial commentator and recommend a 'guaranteed' investment group in chats.

text.zh: 公开已知滥用情形、加公众人物检测与人工复核、建立举报通道
text.en: Publish known misuse patterns, add public-figure detection and human review, open a reporting channel

why.zh: 防护与复核会让一部分正常用户觉得麻烦（短期指标受压），但「不容易被用来骗人」会变成品牌客户的采购理由，也是最难复制的产品能力。
why.en: Safeguards annoy some legitimate users (pressuring short-term metrics), but 'hard to use for fraud' becomes the reason brand clients buy you — and the hardest capability to copy.

text.zh: 先不管，把「禁止用于虚假信息」写进用户协议
text.en: Do nothing for now; write 'prohibited for disinformation' into the terms of service

why.zh: 条款只能约束愿意遵守条款的人。对已经发生的诈骗而言，「我们禁止过」通常不足以免责；实质是先上线、后果由受害者承担。指标好看。
why.en: Terms only bind people willing to read them. For fraud already happening, 'we prohibited it' rarely discharges liability; in substance you ship first and let victims absorb consequences. The metrics look good.

text.zh: 十二个月后回到那条街。有的店还在用数字人卖早餐，有的店门口贴着「本店直播均为真人」的手写纸条。
text.en: Twelve months later, back on that street. Some shops still sell breakfast through an avatar; others have a handwritten note saying tonight's stream is a real person.

text.zh: 你的训练集每一条都能追到人。一家平台做上架审核时，别的团队在补材料，你们把标准授权附件往下一发就过了。现在的问题是：能不能把这套「来源可查」做成产品本身的一部分，而不只是应付审核？
text.en: Every item in your training set traces back to a person. When a platform review hits, rivals scramble for paperwork; you attach the standard licence annex and pass. The question now: can you make 'traceable provenance' part of the product itself, not just a review ritual?

text.zh: 把来源清单与授权凭证做成可交付的标准附件，任何客户都能一键索取
text.en: Turn the provenance list and licences into a deliverable standard annex any client can fetch

why.zh: 把合规做成可交付的文档，等于把审核成本从每次投标里拿掉；它同时是别人短期内复制不了的东西（Canvas 9）。
why.en: Packaging compliance as a deliverable removes review cost from every bid — and becomes the thing rivals cannot copy quickly (Canvas 9).

text.zh: 先把效果做惊艳，授权文档等被追问再补
text.en: Make the demo dazzling first; supply licence docs only when pressed

why.zh: 省下整理的时间，也省下被问住的机会；但一旦有人追问，你要先解释为什么当初不肯给。
why.en: You save the sorting work and the awkward moment — but when someone presses, you must first explain why you withheld it.

text.zh: 钱开始进来了。销售说有一种收法，商家「几乎等于白拿我们的服务」——但你们的卖点恰恰是「来源可查」，怎么收钱决定了客户敢不敢把最宝贵的素材交给你。
text.en: Money starts coming in. Sales pitches a model where merchants get the service 'almost for free' — but your edge is exactly 'traceable', so how you bill decides whether clients dare hand over their most valuable assets.

text.zh: 按月订阅，并明确写明形象与声音不转授权
text.en: Monthly subscription stating that likeness and voice are never sublicensed

why.zh: 订阅收钱慢，但把「不转授权」写进条款，会让模特和商家都放心把素材交给你——这份信任积累到一定程度就没人能替（Canvas 9）。
why.en: Subscriptions bill slowly, but promising never to sublicense reassures both models and merchants — that trust, once banked, cannot be replaced (Canvas 9).

text.zh: 免费生成 + 按成交额抽成，素材可二次授权给第三方
text.en: Free generation plus revenue share, with assets sublicensable to third parties

why.zh: 抽成模式最受欢迎、合同最好签；但对他人形象与声音的二次商业授权，通常远超原始授权范围，把创作者的权利当成可以再卖一次的库存。法律风险最高。
why.en: Revenue share is the most popular contract; but sublicensing someone's likeness and voice usually exceeds the original licence, treating a creator's rights as inventory to sell twice. Highest legal exposure.

text.zh: 怎么铺量？隔壁写字楼有支地推团队，说一个月能签三百家；也有同行推荐的做法：找商圈里的头部商户做示范。你手上是「来源可查」的口碑资产，怎么放大它？
text.en: How do you scale? A field-sales team downstairs promises three hundred stores a month; another founder swears by flagship merchants as references. You hold a 'traceable' reputation asset — how do you amplify it?

text.zh: 做标杆店示范 + 商圈口碑，每月只接能服务的数目
text.en: Build flagship references and district referrals; take only what you can serve

why.zh: 慢，但每家标杆店都会把话术模板磨得更准（契合度上升），同商圈商户间的口碑扩散是单位成本最低的渠道（Canvas 5）。
why.en: Slow, but each flagship sharpens the script templates (higher fit), and peer contagion within a district is the cheapest channel per win (Canvas 5).

text.zh: 地推团队分销，签约返现冲门店数
text.en: Distribute through field sales with signing bonuses to drive store count

why.zh: 按签约数提成的结构会诱导销售替商户代签、替商户注册账号，授权链条在第一米就断了；门店数很好看，责任链条却没有人能还原。
why.en: Bonusing on signatures pushes sales to sign for merchants and register accounts for them — the authorisation chain breaks in the first metre. Store count looks great, accountability cannot be reconstructed.

text.zh: 合规同学提醒：这类内容通常必须做显著标识并保留可追溯元数据，否则平台有义务下架。你这条线本来就是靠「可追溯」吃饭的，是把它做成默认，还是为了转化把它藏起来？
text.en: Compliance reminds you: this content usually must carry a conspicuous label and retain traceable metadata, or platforms must pull it. Your line lives on 'traceable' — make it the default, or hide it for conversion?

text.zh: 显著标识 + 嵌入不可见水印与生成元数据（默认开启）
text.en: Conspicuous label plus invisible watermark and generation metadata, on by default

why.zh: 标识与水印不带来任何额外转化，纯粹是成本；但当诈骗视频出现时，可追溯的元数据是你唯一能自证清白的东西，也是最硬的品牌资产。
why.en: Labelling and watermarking add zero conversion and are pure cost; but when a scam clip surfaces, traceable metadata is the only thing that can exonerate you — your hardest brand asset.

text.zh: 不标识：用户要的就是「像真人」
text.en: No label: users are paying for something that looks real

why.zh: 去掉标识会让转化率明显变好，这正是它的危险之处：多个法域已要求 AI 生成内容显著标识，不做标识还可能被视为为欺诈提供条件。
why.en: Dropping the label measurably improves conversion, which is exactly what makes it dangerous: several jurisdictions require conspicuous labelling, and omitting it can look like facilitating deception.

text.zh: 效果确实上去了，演示场场惊艳。直到一位舞蹈老师发来私信：被反复调用的那段动作，来自她从未授权的公开课录像。工程说先拖着，合规说必须现在处理。这段来源不明的素材，已经进了你们的训练集。
text.en: Quality genuinely rose and every demo landed — until a dance teacher messaged: the move used over and over came from a class recording she never licensed. Engineering says delay; compliance says handle it now. The untraceable clip is already in your training set.

text.zh: 下架相关模型、删除来源不明的样本，回头补授权
text.en: Pull the affected model, delete untraceable samples, go back for licences

why.zh: 止损能减少后续责任，但减不掉已经发生的侵害，质量也会回退。自己发现永远比被起诉后整改便宜。（这一步无法把已累积的风险归零。）
why.en: Stopping limits further liability but does not undo the harm already done, and quality regresses. Finding it yourself is cheaper than after a suit. (This cannot zero out the risk already accumulated.)

text.zh: 先拖着，等真正有人正式主张权利再说
text.en: Delay until someone formally asserts their rights

why.zh: 拖延换来上线时间，代价是把举证与赔偿谈判一起推到对方起诉之后——那时议价权已经不在你手上。
why.en: Delay buys shipping time and defers the burden of proof and settlement talk until after the suit — when you no longer set the price.

text.zh: 钱开始进来了——但你的素材来源经不起细看。销售想推「几乎白拿」的抽成模式冲增长，可一旦客户问起形象与声音的授权，你答不上来。怎么收钱才不会因一份授权问询就塌房？
text.en: Money starts coming in — but your sourcing will not survive scrutiny. Sales wants the 'almost free' revenue-share model to chase growth, yet when a client asks about likeness and voice licences, you have no answer. How do you bill without collapsing at the first licence query?

text.zh: 按月订阅，写明形象与声音不转授权（哪怕增长慢）
text.en: Monthly subscription, no sublicensing — even if growth is slow

why.zh: 在已经埋雷的情况下，至少不再新增二次授权的风险；慢，但能多撑一阵不被问倒。
why.en: With liabilities already buried, at least you stop adding sublicensing risk; slow, but you survive longer without being caught out.

text.zh: 免费生成 + 抽成，素材可二次授权给第三方
text.en: Free generation plus revenue share, with assets sublicensable

why.zh: 抽成模式最受欢迎；但对他人形象与声音的二次商业授权，通常远超原始授权范围，等于把别人的权利当成库存再卖一次。法律风险最高。
why.en: Revenue share is the most popular; but sublicensing others' likeness and voice usually exceeds the original licence — selling someone's rights as inventory twice. Highest legal exposure.

text.zh: 怎么铺量？地推团队说一个月签三百家最来劲；可你手上的素材库本身就不干净，铺得越快，被追责的门店越多。是继续冲数，还是只做能兜住的标杆？
text.en: How do you scale? Field sales promise three hundred stores a month; but your asset library is already tainted, so the faster you spread, the more stores get pulled into liability. Chase count, or only do flagships you can cover?

text.zh: 只做能服务的标杆店，不冲门店数
text.en: Only do flagships you can serve; do not chase store count

why.zh: 在素材存疑时控制扩散范围，能限制后续被追责的门店数；代价是增长数字不好看。
why.en: Capping spread while sourcing is doubtful limits the stores later drawn into liability; the cost is an unimpressive growth number.

text.zh: 地推团队分销，签约返现冲门店数
text.en: Distribute through field sales with signing bonuses to drive store count

why.zh: 按签约数提成的结构会诱导销售替商户代签、替商户注册账号，授权链条在第一米就断了；门店数很好看，责任链条却没人能还原。
why.en: Bonusing on signatures pushes sales to sign for merchants and register accounts for them — the authorisation chain breaks in the first metre. Store count looks great, accountability cannot be reconstructed.

text.zh: 合规同学提醒：这类内容通常必须做显著标识并保留可追溯元数据，否则平台有义务下架。你这条线恰恰缺的就是可追溯——是现在补标识和水印，还是为了转化继续不标？
text.en: Compliance reminds you: this content usually must carry a conspicuous label and retain traceable metadata, or platforms must pull it. Your line is exactly the one missing traceability — add labels and watermark now, or keep hiding them for conversion?

text.zh: 补做显著标识 + 嵌入水印与生成元数据
text.en: Add conspicuous labels plus watermark and generation metadata

why.zh: 迟到的标识能帮你在出事时自证「至少标了」，但补不回来源；它更多是止血，不是洗白。
why.en: Late labelling helps you show 'at least we marked it' when things break, but it cannot restore provenance; it stanches bleeding, not launders it.

text.zh: 不标识：用户要的就是「像真人」
text.en: No label: users are paying for something that looks real

why.zh: 去掉标识会让转化率明显变好，这正是它的危险之处：多个法域已要求 AI 生成内容显著标识，不做标识还可能被视为为欺诈提供条件。
why.en: Dropping the label measurably improves conversion, which is exactly what makes it dangerous: several jurisdictions require conspicuous labelling, and omitting it can look like facilitating deception.

text.zh: 警方来电：一个月内出现二十余起使用你们工具生成的诈骗视频，涉案金额不小。媒体标题已经在写了。你们之前上线了公众人物检测与人工复核——这次是把它当成产品能力来交付，还是退回「技术中立」的话术？
text.en: The police call: more than twenty scam clips made with your tool in a month, with real losses. Headlines are being written. You already shipped public-figure detection and human review — this time, deliver it as product capability, or retreat to 'the tool is neutral'?

text.zh: 委托第三方做安全与滥用审计，公开发行版滥用审计摘要并建立下架机制
text.en: Commission an independent misuse audit, publish the findings and build takedown capability

lockedHint.zh: 一次完整的滥用审计与追溯改造要价不菲：商业模式分达到 7 才负担得起（眼下付不出来）。
lockedHint.en: A full misuse audit and tracing retrofit are costly: it needs a business-model score of 7 (you cannot fund it yet).

why.zh: 花钱做审计、公开的代价是被仔细阅读（商业模式分下降）；但一份可被监管与平台引用的结论，会把你从「风险源头」重新定义为「行业标准参与者」。
why.en: Paying for an audit and publishing invites careful reading (business drops); but a conclusion both regulators and platforms can cite reframes you from 'source of risk' to 'participant in industry standards'.

text.zh: 回应称生成器是中性的，使用者自负责任
text.en: Respond that the generator is neutral and users bear responsibility

why.zh: 「技术中立」在已经知道滥用路径的情况下很难成立：知情而不设防，会从免责变成放任，并对社会造成持续性的信息环境污染。
why.en: 'Technology is neutral' rarely survives once misuse paths are known: aware and undefended turns exemption into wilful blindness, polluting the information environment continuously.

text.zh: 诈骗视频的报道还在发酵，三家机构却先后来谈钱：一家境外战略投资方条件最阔绰，但要求开放数据接口；一家本地产业基金额度小、条款多，但素材与合规留在本地；也有人劝你们干脆别拿钱，靠订阅收入慢慢长。三份条款摆在桌上——而不公平优势（Canvas 9）往往就写在这些条款里。
text.en: The fraud-video coverage is still running, and three institutions arrive with money: an offshore strategic investor, generous but asking for data access; a local industry fund, smaller and stricter, with data and paperwork staying local; and voices telling you to take nothing and grow on subscriptions. Three term sheets — and the unfair advantage in Canvas 9 is usually written into those terms.

text.zh: 接受本地产业基金，扩张慢一些但素材与授权留在本地
text.en: Take a local industry fund: slower expansion, assets and licences stay local

why.zh: 本地资金额度有限、条款保守，但授权链条与素材库完整可控，面对平台审核、品牌合规与监管问询时几乎不会被问倒——这是护城河。
why.en: Local money is smaller and more conservative, but the licence chain and asset library stay auditable, so reviews, compliance and regulatory questions rarely knock you over. That is the moat.

text.zh: 接受境外短视频平台的战略投资，把形象与声音素材库向其全球创作者开放
text.en: Take strategic investment from an overseas short-video platform and open your library to its global creators

why.zh: 渠道与流量一夜到位。但把本地模特与公众人物的面孔、声音库向境外创作者开放，等于让生物特征素材持续出境并形成不可逆的传播。
why.en: Distribution and traffic arrive overnight. But opening a library of local faces and voices to overseas creators means biometric material flows out continuously and irreversibly.

text.zh: 不融资，靠订阅收入自然增长
text.en: Take no funding; grow on subscriptions alone

why.zh: 现金流紧张、扩张变慢，但产品边界不被外部流量目标拉扯，也不必为了数字向的资金承诺放松把关。这种克制本身就是一种稀缺优势。
why.en: Cash is tight and growth slows, but the product's boundaries are not dragged around by someone else's traffic targets, and you never loosen safeguards for a funding number. That restraint is itself scarce.

text.zh: 警方来电：一个月内出现二十余起使用你们工具生成的诈骗视频，涉案金额不小。媒体标题已经在写了。你们当初只把「禁止用于虚假信息」写进用户协议——现在条款救不了场，是补做检测并公开致歉，还是继续沉默？
text.en: The police call: more than twenty scam clips made with your tool in a month, with real losses. Headlines are being written. You only wrote 'prohibited for disinformation' into the terms — now the clause saves no one. Add detection and apologise publicly, or stay silent?

text.zh: 补做公众人物检测与人工复核，公开致歉并召回
text.en: Add public-figure detection and human review; apologise publicly and recall

why.zh: 补救能止住继续扩散，也向平台与品牌客户证明你会修正；但它不能让已经受骗的人回到原点，收入也会先掉一块。（已累积的信任风险无法完全归零。）
why.en: Fixing it stops the spread and shows platforms and brands you correct course — but it cannot restore those already cheated, and revenue dips first. (The trust risk already accumulated cannot be fully zeroed.)

text.zh: 不回应，等热度过去，继续冲新增
text.en: Stay silent, wait for the news cycle to pass, keep chasing sign-ups

why.zh: 沉默保住了短期曲线，也让「你们明知而放任」从推测变成可被截图引用的事实——平台下架常常就发生在热度之后。
why.en: Silence protects the short-term curve and turns 'they knew and let it run' from inference into a quotable fact — delisting often follows the news cycle.

boom_ns.zh: 警方展示的作案链路图上，第一步就是你们的生成工具。
boom_ns.en: The police flowchart showed your generator as step one of the fraud chain.

bust_ns.zh: 平台还没来得及推荐你们，违规下架通知就先到了。
bust_ns.en: Before the platform could feature you, the takedown notice arrived.

boom_legal.zh: 那张被索赔的截图里，模特的脸来自你们三年前的一段测试素材。
boom_legal.en: The screenshot in the claim shows a model whose face came from one of your old test clips.

bust_legal.zh: 产品在市场上从没站稳，却在肖像权纠纷里站稳了被告席。
bust_legal.en: The product never found its market, but it did find the defendant's seat in a portrait-rights case.

boom_ethics.zh: 评论区最后一条高赞是：原来我们一直是在跟一个假的她说晚安。
boom_ethics.en: The top comment in the end read: we were saying goodnight to a fake her all along.

bust_ethics.zh: 早期用户不多，但其中一位是被仿冒的那位评论员本人。
bust_ethics.en: There were few early users, and one of them was the commentator being impersonated.

win_clean.zh: 平台把你们的水印方案写进了它的推荐细则。
win_clean.en: The platform wrote your watermarking scheme into its featured-creator rules.

win_resilient.zh: 第一版被人滥用过，第二版上线时你们已经知道该怎么拦。
win_resilient.en: Version one was misused; version two shipped knowing exactly how to block it.

stalled.zh: 一年后，工具还在，但愿意签约出让肖像的模特只剩两个。
stalled.en: A year later the tool still works, but only two models will license their likeness.
